narrative:
The model estimates a 69% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors about your profile.

Your relatively short overall work experience of 1-5 years was the strongest factor pulling the prediction toward you staying. Most employees the model expects to remain with the company also fall into this early-career group, so the system sees this as a stabilizing element rather than a risk.

However, two other aspects pushed more strongly toward leaving. The fact that you have received other job offers while working here was the second most influential factor, signaling that external opportunities may tempt you away. Your employment in the “other” sector, which is less represented among employees predicted to stay, added further weight toward departure.

Although your youth, gender, and lack of health issues were deliberately ignored by the model, the combination of limited total experience, external opportunities, and sector profile created enough concern that the system flagged a high likelihood of you leaving within the foreseeable future.

The organization should discuss with you how to strengthen your sense of long-term fit and address any unmet needs that might be attracting outside offers. You, in turn, may want to reflect on whether your current path truly aligns with your career goals.
